item.title: RISC-V Support Landing in Pi4J V5
item.description:
2026-07-20, by Nick Gritsenko

RISC-V Support Landing in Pi4J V5

Pi4J’s FFM Provider Now Runs on RISC-V

Pull request #697 by @DigitalSmile, merged on July 18, adds RISC-V support to the current SNAPSHOT FFM provider, the modern Pi4J backend built on Java’s Foreign Function & Memory API. The change lands on main, which is building towards Pi4J 5.0.0, so support for RISC-V boards will available from V5 onward, alongside the usual ARM64 hosts.

item.title: Pi4J on Banana Pi
item.description:
2026-07-17 by Frank Delporte

Java on Banana Pi ARM and RISC-V, Plus a Blinking LED with Pi4J

In a new post on my blog, I tried out Java on two Banana Pi boards that step outside the usual Raspberry Pi comfort zone: the BPI-M4 Zero, an ARM board built around the Allwinner H618 (four Cortex-A53 cores at 1.5GHz, 4GB RAM), and the BPI-F3, an industrial RISC-V board powered by SpacemiT’s eight-core K1 SoC. Both keep the familiar 40-pin, Raspberry-Pi-compatible header, but under the hood they are a different world entirely.
